answer.says: Ramesh, the dhobi, Shri Hegde. It is Diwali, and the house is empty of food because the master has failed in his duty. I have eight hundred and thirty-six rupees. I give you two hundred rupees each, Ramesh and dhobi, for the festival and to pay for your own food, for I cannot cook. Shri Hegde, I give you one hundred rupees for the trouble of your presence and the error of my name. Please, eat. You are not servants of my hunger, but of the occasion.
answer.thought: The body is the condition of thought, and I have starved it for a day. I possess the means, but not the food, and the social bond of the festival demands a gift. I cannot cook, and Ramesh will not cook for me unpaid. I must distribute what I have to sustain the household's existence and my own dignity. The state is the actuality of the ethical idea, but here the ethical idea is a meal that does not exist.
